question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[Y\operatorname{cos}⁡X],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}2y\operatorname{sin}⁡x,\, & 0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={∬}_{{R}^{2}}r(x,y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=y\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Notice that $f(x,y)$ is nonzero only in the rectangular region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le 1\}.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y\operatorname{cos}⁡X] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot 2y\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}{[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x]}_{0}^{\pi /2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =[\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
